answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a lagoon as the anchor of the cost.
